items.title: Lillie Delk Christian Interview, 1961-04-25
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Well, would Florence Mills be regarded as a... she was a show singer, wasn't she? ... [INTERVIEWEE] No. No.

ctx.x: recall just who the popular singers were. Some of those people, now like Ethel Waters, she would mix hers. You know, she'd sing blue melody number, then

she'd sing swing number, you know, something like that. Well, would Florence Mills be regarded as a... she was a show singer, wasn't she? Yeah. Mainly a popular... I tried. Yeah, you wouldn't class her as a blue singer. No. No. And still, you weren't doing musical comedies, so you weren't exactly that same category either way.

That's right. How would Alberta Hunter be? Well, Alberta Hunter, she kind of mixed them up too, see? She sang blues and then popular numbers too. Yeah, I remember her quite well. Did you remember working with any of these girls that we've mentioned? No. When they were working, I wasn't, see? Just like I said, I started out there with Bottoms and 27th, and I quit. I didn't go back no more until 34, see? And, of course, lots of them were still working, but lots of them were working out of the city, in and out, in…
